cleanIntro: The TS 2 is a single-action competition pistol and it strips on a WITNESS-MARK: two vertical lines, one on the frame and one on the slide, must be aligned before the slide stop will come out. ⛔ And the ORANGE is not quite the standard TS 2 — CZ gives it its own instruction: after the recoil spring and guide come out, a SLIDE INSERT has to be removed before the barrel will come forward out of the slide face. ⚠ Two more things this book is firm about: the hammer goes to HALF-COCK first, and the firing pin is kept DRY.

steps.title: ⛔ Magazine OUT — CZ forbids stripping with one inserted
steps.action: Point the pistol in a safe direction and remove the magazine. CZ states it as a prohibition rather than an ordering preference: the pistol must not be disassembled with the magazine inserted.
steps.prose: That is a stronger sentence than most manuals use, and it is the first line of the strip.
steps.quote: 1. Remove the magazine. The pistol must not be disassembled with the magazine inserted!
steps.cite: CZ TS 2 INSTRUCTION MANUAL — 06/2025 (part 735342000002) — Maintenance Instructions — Stripping for Cleaning, step 1, p.9

steps.title: Safety OFF so the slide will move, then LOOK in the chamber
steps.action: Put the safety to the "OFF" position — on this pistol the safety blocks the slide, so it has to come off before anything else moves. Then make certain there is no cartridge in the chamber. CZ prints that step in capitals.
steps.prose: A safety that locks the slide is why the order here is magazine, safety, chamber — and not the order you may be used to.
steps.caution: MAKE SURE THAT THERE IS NO CARTRIDGE IN THE CHAMBER!
steps.quote: 2. Put the safety to "OFF" position, in order to release the movement of the slide.
steps.cite: CZ TS 2 INSTRUCTION MANUAL — 06/2025 (part 735342000002) — Maintenance Instructions — Stripping for Cleaning, step 2, p.9

steps.title: Hammer to the HALF-COCK notch — everything after this is easier
steps.action: Retract the hammer slightly and release it so it stops on the half-cock (safety) notch. CZ's stated reason is practical: in that state the handling that follows is easier. It is not a safety step so much as a geometry one.
steps.prose: Fully down or fully cocked both fight you at the slide stop. Half-cock is the position the rest of the strip is designed around.
steps.quote: 4. Retract the hammer slightly back and then release it, until it stops on half-cock
steps.cite: CZ TS 2 INSTRUCTION MANUAL — 06/2025 (part 735342000002) — Maintenance Instructions — Stripping for Cleaning, step 4, p.9

steps.title: ⛔ ALIGN THE TWO VERTICAL LINES — frame and slide
steps.action: Put your left thumb through the trigger guard and grip the top of the FRONT part of the slide with the other fingers. Push the slide slightly back until the two vertical lines — one on the rear of the frame, one on the slide — line up with each other. ⛔ That alignment is the whole gate: the slide stop will not come out without it.
steps.prose: Thumb through the guard is what gives you a fixed pivot so the slide can be held exactly on the mark rather than near it.
steps.quote: Push the slide slightly back until the two vertical lines on the rear part of the frame and slide are in line with each other (Fig. 7).
steps.cite: CZ TS 2 INSTRUCTION MANUAL — 06/2025 (part 735342000002) — Maintenance Instructions — Stripping for Cleaning, step 5, p.9

steps.title: KEEPING THE LINES ALIGNED, push the slide stop out from the RIGHT
steps.action: Hold the alignment and push the slide stop out from the RIGHT-hand side of the firearm — CZ suggests the corner protrusion on the magazine base as the tool. Then remove the slide stop. ⚠ If it will not move, the lines have drifted; reset rather than pushing harder.
steps.prose: The pistol tells you when it is ready. A slide stop that resists is a slide that is a millimetre off the mark.
steps.quote: 6. KEEPING THE LINES ALIGNED, push the slide stop from the right hand side of the firearm, using the magazine base corner protrusion for example.
steps.cite: CZ TS 2 INSTRUCTION MANUAL — 06/2025 (part 735342000002) — Maintenance Instructions — Stripping for Cleaning, step 6, p.9

steps.title: Slide and barrel FORWARD off the frame
steps.action: With the slide stop out, pull the slide and the barrel forward off the front of the frame together. Then take out the recoil spring and guide — and the sleeve if your pistol has one.
steps.prose: Forward, as a unit. The barrel does not separate from the slide until the next step.
steps.quote: 7. Pull the slide and the barrel forward off the frame.
steps.cite: CZ TS 2 INSTRUCTION MANUAL — 06/2025 (part 735342000002) — Maintenance Instructions — Stripping for Cleaning, step 7, p.9

steps.title: ⛔ ORANGE ONLY — the SLIDE INSERT comes out before the barrel
steps.action: This is the step that is yours and not the standard TS 2's. On the ORANGE variant, once the recoil spring and guide are out you must remove the SLIDE INSERT. Only then does the barrel slide FORWARD out of the slide face.
steps.prose: If you have followed a standard TS 2 walkthrough and the barrel will not come out, this is why — there is a part in the way that the other variants do not have.
steps.quote: *In the case of the ORANGE variant, the removal of the recoil spring and guide shall be followed by removing the slide insert. Then, slide the barrel forward out of the slide face.
steps.cite: CZ TS 2 INSTRUCTION MANUAL — 06/2025 (part 735342000002) — Maintenance Instructions — Stripping for Cleaning, step 8 note, p.9

steps.title: ⚠ That is far enough — no further strip for routine maintenance
steps.action: CZ marks the end of the routine strip here: no further disassembly is needed for routine maintenance. After a great many rounds it is advisable to also clean the firing pin and the magazine — and those are the only two things it adds.
steps.prose: A stated stopping point is worth as much as a step. Past this the book sends you to a gunsmith.
steps.quote: No further disassembly is needed for routine maintenance. When a great number of cartridges have been fired, it is advisable to also clean the firing pin and the magazine.
steps.cite: CZ TS 2 INSTRUCTION MANUAL — 06/2025 (part 735342000002) — Maintenance Instructions — Stripping for Cleaning, p.9
steps.warn: CAUTION: No further disassembly of your pistol is recommended. Should your pistol

steps.title: ⛔ Rod and brush from the CHAMBER, all the way through before reversing
steps.action: The cleaning rod and the brush go into the bore FROM THE CHAMBER — CZ's stated reason is to prevent wear or damage to the muzzle. Pass the brush ALL THE WAY THROUGH before reversing; changing direction with the brush inside can stick it.
steps.prose: Two failures avoided by one habit: a worn crown and a brush jammed halfway down a match barrel.
steps.aside: Pass the brush all the way through the barrel bore before reversing the movement.
steps.quote: The cleaning rod and the brush must be inserted into the barrel bore from the chamber, to prevent wear or damage to the muzzle.
steps.cite: CZ TS 2 INSTRUCTION MANUAL — 06/2025 (part 735342000002) — Cleaning the Barrel Bore and the Cartridge Chamber, p.10

steps.title: Patch until clean; solvent for 10 minutes if it is bad
steps.action: If little has been fired, a clean patch on the rod through bore and chamber, repeated with fresh patches until the last comes out clean. If the bore is very dirty, apply gun cleaning solution with a brush and LET IT ACT ABOUT 10 MINUTES before scrubbing, then dry with a clean patch and check the residues are gone.
steps.prose: The ten minutes is the part people skip, and it is what makes the scrubbing work rather than just moving fouling around.
steps.quote: Let the solvent act for about 10 minutes (this time may vary depending on the solvent agent being used).
steps.cite: CZ TS 2 INSTRUCTION MANUAL — 06/2025 (part 735342000002) — Cleaning the Barrel Bore and the Cartridge Chamber, p.10

steps.title: ⛔ NEVER use bore solvent on the other parts
steps.action: The rest of the pistol — including the barrel's OUTSIDE surfaces — gets a dry cloth, an old toothbrush, a brass bristle brush or a wooden scraper, with preserving or paraffin oil. ⛔ Never an agent designed for bore cleaning: CZ says it can remain in the joints and cause corrosion later. Then check no cloth particles or bristles are lodged anywhere.
steps.prose: This is the sentence that separates a clean pistol from one that quietly corrodes from the inside of its own joints.
steps.quote: Never use an agent designed for barrel bore cleaning. These solutions could remain in the joints, and after some time could cause corrosion.
steps.cite: CZ TS 2 INSTRUCTION MANUAL — 06/2025 (part 735342000002) — Cleaning of Other Pistol Parts, p.10

steps.title: ⛔ Keep the FIRING PIN dry — and check the BUFFER every clean
steps.action: Do NOT lubricate the firing pin assembly or the firing pin opening in the slide; keep them dry and clean. ⚠ And after EVERY cleaning, check the buffer: if it is visibly deformed or its contact surface is cut, it must be replaced.
steps.prose: A wet firing pin channel on a competition pistol collects fouling and slows the pin. The buffer check is a wear item on a schedule of every clean, which is unusual and worth honouring.
steps.aside: After every cleaning, check the condition of the buffer. If it is visibly deformed or its contact surface cut, it shall be replaced.
steps.quote: Do not lubricate the firing pin assembly and the firing pin opening in the slide; keep them dry and clean.
steps.cite: CZ TS 2 INSTRUCTION MANUAL — 06/2025 (part 735342000002) — Firing Pin Disassembly, p.9

steps.title: Oil everything, then WIPE THE BORE DRY before shooting
steps.action: When bore, chamber and all accessible parts are clean and dry, wipe them with a cloth soaked in gun oil or spray it on, and remove ALL excess. ⛔ Before shooting, always wipe the barrel bore DRY. ⚠ At very low temperatures take the oil off all accessible parts, or use a lubricant made for those conditions.
steps.prose: Oil in a bore is a pressure problem, not a lubrication one. The wipe-dry is the last thing you do before the pistol is loaded.
steps.quote: Before shooting always wipe the barrel bore dry.
steps.cite: CZ TS 2 INSTRUCTION MANUAL — 06/2025 (part 735342000002) — Preserving, p.11

deepSteps.title: ⚠ Firing pin — SPRING-LOADED, and it can fly out
deepSteps.action: Push the rear end of the firing pin in with a suitable tool, below the level of the firing pin stop, and shift the stop about 2 mm DOWN. Then COVER the stop with your thumb so the spring-loaded firing pin cannot escape, and pull the stop completely off the slide with the other hand. ⛔ CZ warns the pin could fly out, get lost, or cause injury.
deepSteps.prose: Thumb over the stop before the second hand moves. That is the whole technique, and it is why this is a two-handed job.
deepSteps.caution: Do it over a tray or a towel. A lost firing pin is a pistol out of action.
deepSteps.quote: Then cover the firing pin stop with your thumb in order not to lose the spring-loaded firing pin and with the other hand pull the firing pin stop completely off the slide.
deepSteps.cite: CZ TS 2 INSTRUCTION MANUAL — 06/2025 (part 735342000002) — Firing Pin Disassembly, p.9

deepSteps.title: ⚠ Magazine base — the spring is under load too
deepSteps.action: Push the base lock where it sticks out through the hole in the base and slide the base about 5 mm TOWARDS THE FRONT of the magazine. Cover the base with your thumb to keep the magazine spring, and take the base off its guiding rails with the other hand. ⛔ Same hazard: the spring can fly out or cause injury.
deepSteps.prose: Forward, not down, and 5 mm — far enough to clear the lock and no further.
deepSteps.aside: Cover the base with your thumb to prevent losing the magazine spring and with the other hand take off the base from its guiding rails.
deepSteps.quote: To remove the magazine base, push on the base lock which sticks out through
deepSteps.cite: CZ TS 2 INSTRUCTION MANUAL — 06/2025 (part 735342000002) — Magazine Disassembly, p.10

deepSteps.title: The cleaning SCHEDULE CZ actually publishes
deepSteps.action: CZ gives a condition list rather than a round count: clean the pistol each time you use it; if you get it wet; as soon as possible after shooting; at least once a year in a temperate climate; and as often as once a month in a tropical climate or other demanding environment.
deepSteps.prose: Five triggers, and the last two are about storage rather than shooting — which is the half people forget.
deepSteps.quote: Cleaning the Pistol Clean the pistol - Each time you use it - If you get your pistol wet - As soon as possible after shooting - At least once a year in a temperate climate - As often as once a month in a tropical climate, or other demanding environment
deepSteps.cite: CZ TS 2 INSTRUCTION MANUAL — 06/2025 (part 735342000002) — Cleaning the Pistol, p.10

deepSteps.title: ⚠ Preserving grease is for STORAGE only, and must come off first
deepSteps.action: Thick preserving agents such as preserving grease are only for long-term storage in demanding climates, and before ANY use of the pistol the grease must be thoroughly removed from all parts.
deepSteps.prose: Grease left in a competition pistol is a malfunction waiting for the first cold morning.
deepSteps.quote: Use thick preserving agents such as preserving grease only for a long-term storage in demanding climate environments, and before any use of the pistol it must be thoroughly removed from all parts of the firearm.
deepSteps.cite: CZ TS 2 INSTRUCTION MANUAL — 06/2025 (part 735342000002) — Preserving, p.11

cleaning.name: BARREL BORE AND CHAMBER
tasks: ⛔ Rod and brush enter FROM THE CHAMBER — never the muzzle
Brush passed all the way through before reversing
Patches until the last one comes out clean
Solvent left to act about 10 minutes on a very dirty bore, then scrubbed
Dried with a clean patch and checked for remaining residue

cleaning.name: EVERYTHING ELSE
tasks: Dry cloth, old toothbrush, brass bristle brush or wooden scraper
⛔ NEVER a bore-cleaning agent — it stays in the joints and corrodes
Checked for lodged cloth particles and brush bristles

cleaning.name: FIRING PIN AND BUFFER
tasks: ⛔ Firing pin assembly and its opening kept DRY — no lubricant
Firing pin and magazine cleaned after a great many rounds
⚠ Buffer inspected after EVERY cleaning; replaced if deformed or cut

cleaning.name: PRESERVING
tasks: Gun oil on clean, dry parts; all excess removed
Oil removed at very low temperatures, or a cold-rated lubricant used
Preserving grease for long-term storage only, and fully removed before use

reassembly: ⛔ ORANGE: slide insert back in BEFORE the recoil spring and guide.
Barrel into the slide from the front; recoil spring and guide (and sleeve if fitted).
Slide and barrel onto the frame from the front.
Two vertical lines aligned, slide stop pushed in from the LEFT and seated.
Buffer condition confirmed — replaced if deformed or its contact surface cut.
Bore wiped DRY before any live round.
fncheck: Magazine out, chamber checked by eye. Confirm the slide stop is fully seated and the two witness lines are no longer aligned once the slide is forward — a slide stop sitting proud is the failure this strip invites. Cycle the slide through full travel and let it run into battery; check the safety locks the slide with the hammer cocked, and that the half-cock notch catches. ⛔ Then wipe the bore dry, and check the buffer if this was a cleaning — CZ asks for that after every one.
